title: Lavender and honey tart
subtitle: Provençal-style honey tart with culinary lavender
excerpt: A lavender and honey tart sets a gentle honey custard in a buttery pastry case, with culinary lavender infused into the cream before the custard is assembled. The result is floral, sweet, and lightly aromatic, the lavender level should be present but subtle, not medicinal. Too much lavender in a dessert makes it taste of soap; this recipe is calibrated to stay on the right side of that line.
sourceNotes: Honey tarts are a traditional Provençal preparation, associated with the lavender-growing regions of southern France where lavender honey (miel de lavande) is produced commercially. The combination of honey and lavender in a custard tart appears in old Provençal recipe books and continues in the repertoire of French regional pâtisserie. The same tart is also made without lavender in the north of France, where honey alone is the flavour. The key technical point, infusing the lavender in warm cream before straining, is the standard approach for all culinary lavender applications, as direct grinding or adding uninfused dried flowers produces a harsh, floral-soap flavour.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten on the day it is made; serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.temperatureNote: for the custard fill; blind bake the case first at 190°C

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: 160°C conventional (140°C fan) for the custard; 190°C for the blind bake

content.text: Lavender and honey tart has a gentle, floral custard. Infuse the dried lavender in warm cream and strain it out before making the custard. This is the only way to use culinary lavender without the flavour turning soapy. Use exactly 1 teaspoon of dried culinary lavender for this quantity of cream. More than that and the taste becomes unpleasant.

items.prepNote: lavender honey or other light flower honey

content.text: Make the pastry, chill, and blind bake at 190°C using the same method as other tarts in this collection, beans for 15 minutes, then 10 minutes without. Cool before filling.

Combine the cream, milk, and lavender in a small saucepan. Heat over a low flame until the mixture just reaches a simmer, then remove from the heat. Cover and leave to infuse for 15 minutes. Strain through a fine sieve and discard the lavender. Stir in the honey until dissolved.

Preheat the oven to 160°C conventional (140°C fan). Whisk the egg yolks and whole egg together, then pour the warm lavender cream over them in a steady stream, whisking as you go. Pour the custard into the cooled pastry case. Bake for 28 to 32 minutes until just set with a slight wobble in the centre. Leave to cool on a wire rack. Serve warm or at room temperature with a little extra honey drizzled over.
